problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}3 & -6 \\ 2 & -4 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ shown above. If the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is 

$$
[\begin{aligned}a \\ 0\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}b \\ c\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R,
$$

what is the value of  $17a+\frac{b}{c}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Finding the Solution to a Weighted Least-Squares Problem
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14073770/assets/2429c49383a8610e76edcee474205d1f261fc81d1ec65ac4178ebc60f3c6d8d8.png)

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $\mathbf{b}$ shown above. Find the general solution for the weighted least-squares problem $W\!A\mathbf{x}=W\mathbf{b}.$
examples.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\!A\mathbf{x}=W\mathbf{b},$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\!A)^T{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14073770/assets/6607f2839cfc50abcf9a25f0cd22319042c29009fec90ffef35e43d8f24b5be7.png)

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 9\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ -8 & 8 \\ -4 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 0 \\ 36\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}21 & -21 \\ -21 & 21\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-39 \\ 39\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}21 & -21 & -39 \\ -21 & 21 & 39\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}21 & -21 & -39 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, $x_2$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we have 

$$
x_1=-\dfrac{13}{7}+x_2.
$$

Hence, the general solution is

feedback.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 4 & -6 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,W=[\begin{aligned}2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $W,$ and the vector $b$ above. If the normal equation for the corresponding weighted least-squares problem $W\,Ax=Wb$ is given by

$$
[\begin{aligned}a & -42 \\ -42 & b\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}c \\ 36\end{aligned}]
$$

what is the value of $a+b+c?$
feedback.worked_solution:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\,Ax=Wb,$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\,A)^{T}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

$$
{W}^{T}W=[\begin{aligned}{2}^{2} & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & {1}^{2} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & {1}^{2}\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}],
$$

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & 2 \\ 3 & -6 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 4 & -6 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & 2 \\ 3 & -6 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}-2 & 4 & 2 \\ 3 & -6 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-8 & 12 \\ 4 & -6 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-8 & 4 & 2 \\ 12 & -6 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}36 & -42 \\ -42 & 81\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-16 \\ 36\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=36+81+(-16)=101.
$$
